SAIL-Bhilai Steel Plant Launches 'CO₂ Dashboard' to Accelerate Carbon Emission Reduction and Decarbonization Efforts
articles.full_content:
Dashboard enables daily monitoring, analysis, and corrective actions for carbon emissions at both plant and shop levels
In a major step toward accelerating decarbonization efforts and ensuring sustainable operations, Steel Authority of India Limited’s (SAIL) Bhilai Steel Plant (BSP) launched a specially designed 'CO₂ Dashboard' for Bhilai Steel Plant and Chandrapur Ferro Alloy Plant (CFP), Chandrapur. The digital platform was officially inaugurated by Shri Chittaranjan Mahapatra, Director I/c (Bhilai Steel Plant), during a special event held on 18th August 2026. The occasion was attended by Shri Rakesh Kumar, Executive Director (Works); Shri P. Murugesan, Executive Director (CFP Chandrapur); Shri Rajiv Pandey, Executive Director (EMD, Kolkata); along with senior Chief General Managers and officers from BSP, CFP, and EMD-Kolkata.
Developed in collaboration with M/s Centra World, a consultant appointed by the Environment Management Division (EMD, Kolkata), the dashboard aims to enable real-time tracking and management of carbon emissions across the enterprise. It provides accurate tracking and analysis of daily CO₂ emissions at both the plant and individual shop levels. By identifying anomalies promptly, the system allows for quick corrective measures that enhance overall operational efficiency while driving down carbon emissions across production units.
The digital platform assesses emissions in accordance with global standards, including the World Steel Association (WSA) methodology, the GHG Protocol, and the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). In the context of India’s evolving carbon market, the dashboard will play a vital role in helping SAIL align with the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) by assisting units in monitoring emission-intensity targets and preparing for market mechanisms. Furthermore, shop-level and product-level monitoring will strengthen the global competitiveness of SAIL's steel products in international markets.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Chittaranjan Mahapatra, Director I/c (BSP), emphasized that reducing greenhouse gas emissions is not merely a regulatory requirement, but a collective responsibility toward environmental protection and a sustainable future. Shri Rakesh Kumar, Executive Director (Works), highlighted that adherence to process discipline, technical standards, and quality parameters yields a dual benefit by boosting productivity while lowering costs and emissions. Shri P. Murugesan, Executive Director (CFP Chandrapur), and Shri Rajiv Pandey, Executive Director (EMD Kolkata), further stressed that reliable, standardized digital data enables targeted decision-making and timely interventions across all operating units. Ms. Ajanta Sengupta highlighted that the dashboard translates the vision of the SAIL Chairman into a simple, user-friendly tool for top management, while Shri K. Praveen, General Manager (Environment Management), conducted the proceedings and expressed gratitude to all p

Rashtriya Raksha University Launches Master’s in Financial and Economic Security (MFES) Programme Cohort 2.0 in Collaboration with Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Ministry of Corporate Affairs
articles.full_content:
Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), an Institution of National Importance under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, engaged with the media in Bengaluru to highlight the second cohort of its flagship Masters in Financial and Economic Security (MFES) programme, a specialised hybrid programme for working professionals, offered in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India.
The MFES Cohort 2.0 marks a significant step forward in RRU’s endeavour to build a specialised professional ecosystem equipped with the knowledge, investigative capabilities and security-oriented understanding required to address the increasingly sophisticated nature of financial and economic crimes in an evolving digital and interconnected financial landscape.
The programme adopts a multidisciplinary and practice-oriented approach, integrating law, finance, investigation, regulation, emerging technologies and economic security through real-world case studies, analytical tools and expert-led learning. The hybrid learning model enables working professionals to balance advanced education with professional commitments while fostering meaningful engagement with experts and networks across law enforcement, regulatory agencies, financial institutions, corporate organisations and the wider RRU–IICA ecosystem.
Speaking about the programme, Prof. (Dr.) Bimal N. Patel, Vice Chancellor, Rashtriya Raksha University, remarked “Financial and economic security is no longer a specialised concern limited to financial institutions; it is increasingly integral to national security, economic resilience and public trust.” He further emphasised that MFES reflects RRU’s vision of connecting learning with purpose, by developing skilled practitioners who can understand emerging threats, respond with expertise and contribute to safeguarding financial integrity.
Mr. Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General and CEO, Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs, stated, “The Masters in Financial and Economic Security is a flagship collaboration between IICA and RRU, created to respond to the evolving challenges of financial and economic crimes. Through advanced analytical tools, legal expertise, investigative techniques and practical learning, the programme seeks to build future leaders equipped to safeguard economic integrity and contribute to a more secure and prosperous future.”
With the launch of MFES Cohort 2.0, RRU and IICA reaffirm their commitment to strengthening India’s pool of specialized workforce in financial and economic security and nurturing skilled practitioners who can anticipate emerging risks, respond effectively and contribute to a secure, resilient and transparent economic environment

Historic Turnout Marks West Bengal’s First-Ever Kaushal Mahotsav in Balurghat hosted by Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
articles.full_content:
Over 4500 youth shortlisted and more than 7500 interviews conducted
Drawing enthusiastic participation from thousands of aspiring youths, the Kaushal Mahotsav in Balurghat emerged as a major platform connecting job seekers from Dakshin Dinajpur and neighbouring regions with employment opportunities. Organized by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India in collaboration with the Government of West Bengal and the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), the Mahotsav witnessed a historic turnout with over 7500 interviews being conducted. More than 7,000 job opportunities from over 50+ employers provided diverse opportunities to the local youth aspiring to build their careers in different sectors, including manufacturing, retail, logistics, healthcare, hospitality, food processing, banking and financial services, and other services.
The event was attended by Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, Minister of State for Education and Minister of State for Development of Northeastern Region, Government of India; Shri Kshudiram Tudu, Minister – In – Charge, Tribal Development Department, Minority Affairs and Madrasah Education Department, Government of West Bengal; Shri Joyel Murmu, Minister of State, Irrigation and waterways department and Tribal Development Department, Government of West Bengal; Shri Khagen Murmu, Member of Parliament for Malda North; Shri Bidyut Kumar Roy, Member of Legislative Assembly, Balurghat; Shri Badurai Tudu, Member of Legislative Assembly, Tapan; Shri Satyendranath Roy, Member of Legislative Assembly, Gangarampur; Shri Rajiv Kumar, Principal Secretary, Technical Education, Training and Skill Development, Government of West Bengal; Shri VS Arvind, Director, MSDE; Shri Balasubramanium T., District Magistrate, Dakshin Dinajpur; and Shri Abhishek Gupta, Superintendent of Police, Dakshin Dinajpur.
Highlighting that education and skills serve as twin pillars of employability and success, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, Minister of State for Education and Minister of State for Development of Northeastern Region, Government of India, said, “the Skill India Mission was envisioned by our Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi to ensure the youth of India are skilled and are provided a platform to connect with gainful employment opportunities and Kaushal Mahotsav is one such initiative under his guidance.”
Encouraging productive use of technology, he urged them to harness digital platforms and transform their mobile phones into gateways for learning and growth rather than mere sources of entertainment, calling upon the youth to adopt a culture of lifelong learning and skill development.
He further lauded the efforts of Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, for organizing the Kaushal Mahotsav in Balurghat. MSME DFO Dimapur organize PM Vishwakarma One-Day Awareness Workshop on Branding and Marketing in Wokha
articles.full_content:
The MSME Development and Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Dimapur, under the Ministry of MSME, Government of India, in association with the Department of Industries and Commerce and the District Industries Centre (DIC), Wokha, organized a one-day awareness workshop on Branding and Marketing at the DC Conference Hall, Wokha on August 18, 2026, under the PM Vishwakarma scheme.
The workshop aimed to strengthen the entrepreneurial capabilities of PM Vishwakarma artisans by providing practical knowledge on product packaging, labelling and design, business development, export development, Artificial Intelligence (AI), e-commerce, QR code generation and financial literacy. Over 97 artisans, including tailors, carpenters, barbers and basket makers, participated in the programme from across the district.
The programme commenced with a welcome address delivered by Shri K. Myingthungo Kikon, General Manager, DIC Wokha. The keynote address was delivered by Shri K. Mathung Tsanglao, NCS, Deputy Commissioner of Wokha, who addressed participants and highlighted the workshop's vital role in empowering local artisans. He emphasized the importance of building market knowledge and leveraging e-commerce platforms, encouraging artisans to embrace modern marketing approaches to boost their visibility, reach wider customer bases, and grow their businesses. During the event, under his chairmanship, loan sanctions were officially announced for two artisans—a basket maker and a carpenter—under the Central Bank of India, Wokha Branch.
The first technical session on Product Packaging, Labelling and Design was delivered by Smt. Therali Ovung, Proprietor, The Sewist Design Studio and Training Centre, Wokha. The session focused on product development based on customer needs and market demand, highlighting the importance of effective packaging, labelling, product design, and branding.
An interactive session on Business Development was conducted by Smt. Bwenye Kemp, Financial Analyst, RAMP. The session covered business planning, SMART targets, networking, digital business development, identifying product strengths and Unique Selling Propositions (USP), understanding target customers and appropriate pricing strategies.
The Artificial Intelligence and E-commerce Onboarding session was conducted by the State Programme Management Unit (SPMU), PM Vishwakarma wherein the participants were introduced to emerging digital technologies and their applications in product promotion, marketing and enterprise development.
The session on Export Development was conducted by Shri Mhachan N. Kikon, Functional Manager, DIC Wokha, who provided insights into export readiness, accessing international markets and available Government support schemes. The QR Code Generation session was conducted by Smt. Ronbeni C. Lotha, Executive, India Post Payments Bank, Wokha Branch, who highlighted DBT account opening and its benefits under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme.
